questions.prompt: What is the relative formula mass of calcium hydroxide, $\text{Ca(OH)}_2$? (Ca = 40, O = 16, H = 1)
questions.explanation: Everything inside the bracket is multiplied by 2: $40 + 2(16 + 1) = 40 + 34 = 74$.

questions.prompt: How many moles of magnesium atoms are there in 4.8 g of magnesium? (Mg = 24)
What volume, in dm³, does 11 g of carbon dioxide ($\text{CO}_2$) occupy at room temperature and pressure? (C = 12, O = 16; molar volume = 24 dm³)
Which of these samples contain exactly **one mole** of the stated particles? (H = 1, C = 12, O = 16; molar volume at r.t.p. = 24 dm³) Select all that apply.

choices.text: 24 dm³ of nitrogen gas at r.t.p.

questions.explanation: C: $12 \div 12 = 1$ mol. $\text{H}_2\text{O}$: $18 \div 18 = 1$ mol. Any gas: $24 \div 24 = 1$ mol. But $M(\text{O}_2) = 32$, so 16 g is 0.5 mol, and $M(\text{H}_2) = 2$, so 1 g is 0.5 mol.

questions.prompt: One mole of water and one mole of carbon have the same mass.
questions.explanation: They contain the same **number** of particles ($6.02 \times 10^{23}$), but one mole of water has a mass of 18 g and one mole of carbon has a mass of 12 g.

questions.prompt: The number $6.02 \times 10^{23}$, the number of particles in one mole, is called the ______ constant.
questions.explanation: It is the **Avogadro constant**, $N_A = 6.02 \times 10^{23}$ per mole.
